messages:
erin: Noticed a small but consistent bump in host CPU and p95 on tiny streaming requests after the kernel packing rollout. P95 +22ms for <=128 token streams.

sam: Saw same on staging. Flamegraph points at tokenize_utf8 -> memcpy -> writev -> grpc::Write. writev calls/request jumped from ~2 to ~6.

nora: Kernel selector now groups more variants per worker which seems to increase multiplexing across KV shards. KV hit-rate dropped ~3.1%.

erin: Quick plan: (1) enable batcher.prefers_kv_affinity=true on canary, (2) enable proxy.coalesce_small_writes=true with 5ms/16KB window, (3) add microbench to assert writev calls/request <=3 for small streams.

sam: I prototyped coalescing in proxy: buffers per leader and flushes combined writev. Local bench: writev/request -> 1.7, p95 improved ~18ms but median +3ms. Will guard behind flag.

nora: I'll flip kv_affinity flag in canary and add kvcache.evictions_by_worker metric. If evictions spike we can revert quickly.

perf-bot: Regression alert: host-ingress-tokenize CPU +7% vs baseline (24h).

canary-bot: starting canary: packer-affinity-coalesce (id: canary-586789A) monitor /dash/host/streaming

erin: If canary looks good after 30m we'll roll 25% then 2h. Follow-up: PERF-1102 to remove extra memcpy in tokenize_utf8 and add unit test for tokenizer syscall counts.

sam: Watching p95 and writev metric; will report in 15m.

erin: Thanks — tagging oncall if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
